title: Partition pruning, and the query that ignores the partitioning

videos.script: Lesson 17 cut the events table into months. This lesson asks what that bought. {{months}} A query about one day of November should read November and nothing else. When it does, the planner has pruned the other months out of the plan. {{prune}} You see it happen twice. Once while the query is planned, from the dates written in it. And once while it runs, from a value nobody knew in advance. {{twice}} Then the queries that defeat it. A date function wrapped around the column. A filter on the customer instead of the time. Each one reads every partition, and returns the right answer, so nothing warns you. {{defeat}} Then the price of too many partitions. The same rows cut into three hundred and sixty-five days, and a query that now spends thirty milliseconds just making its plan. {{many}} And last, two settings that let the planner work partition by partition, and the one condition they need. {{partitionwise}}
